AUTHOR: Ayyagari
TITLE: Dataset selection is critical for effective pre-training of fish detection models for underwater video
REGION: Canada (DFO custom dataset, Atlantic groundfish; 200-500 m depth; exact location not stated); OOD test on Brackish dataset (Denmark)
SPECIES: Generic 'fish' detector; custom dataset contains Gadus morhua, Macrourus berglax, skate, Sebastes mentella, Anarhichas lupus, Hippoglossus hippoglossus
DATA: Custom DFO underwater video dataset (221 videos, 110,157 frames with fish; fine-tuning subsets of 500 and 1000 frames); pre-training on OzFish, Norfisk, NPSNF, MS COCO; OOD test on Brackish
V_EV: Datasets: 'underwater images with a resolution of 1080 × 1920, captured at depths of 200–500 m'; Discussion: 'deep underwater images of fish under battery-powered lighting'
D2: Custom dataset: 221 videos split 70/15/15 (71,736 / 19,211 / 19,210 frames); fine-tuning subsets of 500 and 1000 training frames; pre-training datasets split randomly by image 70/20/10 or 60/20/20
D_EV: Fine-tuning dataset: 'These 221 videos are segmented into train, validation, and test splits in a 70-15-15 ratio based on the frequency of fish in a frame within each video.'
R_EV: Datasets: 'the Brackish dataset was designated for out-of-distribution (OOD) testing'; Table 6 reports mAP on Brackish separately
C_EV: Training: 'We use the default IoU and confidence thresholds of 0.65 and 0.001, respectively, to train and evaluate the detectors.'
E_EV: Tables 4, 6, 7 report only mAP and per-class recall; Discussion: 'achieving state-of-the-art results in terms of mAP was not the primary focus'
ARCH: YOLOv7 (default hyperparameters), pre-trained on OzFish / Norfisk / NPSNF / MS COCO or random initialisation, fine-tuned on custom dataset
METR: mAP (IoU 0.65, conf 0.001), per-class recall, epochs to convergence, t-tests over 5 runs
NOTE: Split statement is ambiguous: 'These 221 videos are segmented into train, validation, and test splits ... based on the frequency of fish in a frame within each video' is read as videos assigned to splits (stratified by fish frequency), but it could mean frames within each video were split; if the latter, D1 = 이미지/프레임 무작위 and D_ALL = N. Frames extracted at 30 fps so near-duplicates are abundant; no de-duplication mentioned. Public pre-training datasets were split randomly at image level. PLAT not stated in text (metadata hint: fixed fisheries survey camera, low light); depth 200-500 m with artificial lighting gives ENV = 심해. PRE coded 수중 데이터셋 since the study's main comparison is marine pre-training (OzFish best), but COCO and random init are also evaluated. CODE = Y refers to YOLOv7 weights for the public datasets hosted on Hugging Face; custom data available on request. OOD performance on Brackish is very low (mAP < 0.13) but is reported separately (R3 = Y). The dataset catalog (Table 1) is a secondary contribution.
